name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,162

clue.text: In the morning ex-president put together attack

blocks.note: AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon
either George Bush, former US president

explanation.surface: A former president plotted an assault one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put together' only tells you to join the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise assault from a hidden position is a kind of attack, and both words work as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Once more a villein upset Henry

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down entry the letters turn the other way up

blocks.note: taken as written
a villein was a feudal peasant tied to the land, a serf
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A medieval peasant angers King Henry all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a king but is the unit of inductance, whose symbol is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anew, starting over from the beginning, is doing it again: both are adverbs of repetition.

clue.text: Relocate cabins despite assortment of things

indicators.note: to relocate is to move things to new places, so the letters are set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to move the cabins anyway, along with a mixed bag of belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite' reads as a linking preposition, but its letters are part of the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a miscellaneous collection of small odds and ends.

clue.text: Classifying gold gathered in police operation

indicators.note: something gathered in is taken inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a sting is an undercover police trap

explanation.surface: Police sort through recovered gold seized in a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging items into groups by type is classifying them; both are present participles.

blocks.note: first meaning: a source of mineral water
second meaning: the time of year between winter and summer

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a holiday-brochure phrase, but each is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural source of mineral water gave resort towns their name, and the word also names the warming quarter of the year.

indicators.note: saying something loudly means it is heard rather than read, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to faze is to disconcert or worry; the two spellings are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone frets noisily about a stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of a word meaning 'disconcert' gives a differently spelt word for a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage or distinct stretch of time in a process is a period; both are nouns.

indicators.note: done roughly means handled without care, so the letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A speaker would crudely shut down a dreadful insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' seems to mean approximately, but it signals that the letters before it are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too extreme to be put into words cannot be spoken of: both adjectives describe the beyond-words.

clue.text: Politicians start to glean rising expression of contempt

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the order turns around

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a sneer is a scornful look or remark

explanation.surface: Politicians begin to gather a growing show of scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' sounds like growing contempt, but in a down clue it means read the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of environmentalist parties are called Greens, so they are an example of politicians.

clue.text: Socialist accepting flag is no long working

definitions.note: the clue's 'no long' is a misprint for 'no longer'

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: red is the colour of socialism
to flag is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A left-winger who takes up a banner is out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to weaken. The printed 'no long' should read 'no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped their career permanently, typically through age, is described as having left employment.

clue.text: Attractive person on East Street is untrustworthy

blocks.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation
ST is the address abbreviation

explanation.surface: A handsome stranger living on East Street can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is taken literally as two letters rather than as a positional instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given to lying or cheating cannot be relied on; both adjectives describe deceitful character.

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for date, taken twice
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Two romantic evenings over drinks leave someone confused.
explanation.walkthrough: D for date is a standard abbreviation, so two dates are two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse or befuddle someone's thinking is to muddle it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Moved through water with one religious leader

blocks.note: past tense of swim
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone went swimming alongside a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: One becomes I by the Roman numeral convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu ascetic or spiritual teacher bears this title, making it an example of a religious leader.

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a teacher's pets are favourites
to sin is to transgress or offend

explanation.surface: Someone intervenes when the favoured ones come back and cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offend' is used in the old sense of doing wrong, as in sinning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to get involved in a situation to help or settle it, the same as intervening.

clue.text: Part of vicar’s garb involved coral and gold

indicators.note: something involved is intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman's outfit features an intricate pattern of coral and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' here is taken as its letters, not converted to OR as crossword habit suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white band worn around a cleric's neck is the slang name for a clerical collar, a feature of the clothing.

clue.text: Having little to say as the French swindle leaders of international committee

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'
a con is a swindle
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped figure stays quiet while the French cheat the heads of a global committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' points to a French article, here the feminine LA rather than LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse person who uses very few words is described this way; both describe being sparing with speech.

blocks.note: first meaning: knocks over, upsets the contents of
second meaning: thin strips of wood or paper used as tapers

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is an old-fashioned household word for a taper, a sliver of wood or twisted paper lit from a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for knocking liquid over and a noun for slender tapers used to carry a flame.

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: mothers are parents
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Mums and dads take a minute's break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like adding, but here it means taking away.
explanation.definitionFit: The remaining people or things in a group are the remainder, so the plural pronoun matches the noun.

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
liable means apt or likely

explanation.surface: Those with power will probably bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Likely to' reads as a phrase, but 'to be' is only the link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that bends easily without breaking, or a person easily influenced, is supple; both are adjectives.

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone was told to take a high grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good mark' looks like a school grade, but the words split: good is one letter and mark is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem worn to show rank or membership is a distinguishing sign, so a mark in that sense.

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a dog that snapped bit

explanation.surface: A police officer took a photo of an antique unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman and 'snapped' like a photograph, but they give a chemical symbol and a past tense of biting.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient unit based on forearm length, used in the Bible, is a historical measure of length.

clue.text: Transparent top covers middle of saucer

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central part, so only the centre letters are kept
covering means going over and around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a lid is the top of a container
the two central letters of a six-letter word

explanation.surface: A clear lid sits over a saucer.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-letter word has a two-letter middle, so both central letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and easily understood, as in lucid prose, is a figurative sense of see-through, so the adjectives match.

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to enable is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A time-limited licence can be defended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a noun, a licence, but is used as the verb to allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A position able to be held or defended against argument is defensible, which is the same as justifiable.

indicators.note: the exterior is the outside, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
to stem is to staunch a flow, as of blood

explanation.surface: An outwardly loyal institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like the adjective meaning loyal, but is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordered arrangement or method of working is an organisation in the sense of structured arrangement.

blocks.note: first meaning: squeezes money out of someone
second meaning: British slang for jail warders

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British slang: inmates call prison guards by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to extract money by pressure, and the plural noun is slang for jail warders.
